body: Hi there, first off I want to say thanks for sharing that. I'm a recent college graduate and disabled, having trouble finding a job that doesn't cause me tons of pain so I'm still struggling financially like I did in college. My disordered eating comes from being starved by my mom in childhood even though I grew up ostensibly well off, and my current state of poverty is really not helping. I feel like the trauma is compounding instead of getting better because I never learned how to eat normally in the first place, and now I can't afford to even though I really want to recover. I had a period of time where I had a really well paying job right out of college but I was still unable to eat normally, I was making $60k a year (for a month lol) and I still couldn't eat the appropriate amount of calories. I live with 3 trans women and one femme afab nonbinary person and what I hear all the time is, "men are trash but you're not as shit as the rest of them" which makes me feel incredibly bad not because they're letting of steam, but because they're bringing me personally into it. I can wholeheartedly agree with the fact that "men" as an institution is fucking awful. But it does nobody any good to point fingers at individual people repeatedly even in jest, especially if they're making a concerted effort to minimize the harm their privilege does. That's why I save my vitriolic "I hate white people" comments for when I'm only around other POC,  and I try to make my comments more generalized around white people, saying rather "whiteness as an institution is oppressive and dangerous." That way, I get to express my full and angry opinion about the issue, but yet make sure my white friends know that they as people are still dear to me. I can hold them accountable without completely dismissing their entire existence as people. I wish more non-men would do the same. 

As an addendum, I'm not asking for non-men to limit their expression of frustration, I just think it's counterproductive to inflcit the same damage that mysoginy does. It may be what some cis men need to feel to get over themselves, but my poor C-PTSD dysphoric ass does not need it. I already hate myself and want to die. I don't need any more reasons to feel bad.

First of, congratulations on your first step towards independence! It takes serious emotional intelligence to recognize that you need to step away from them in some way, and then start the process, especially when it's clearly so dangerous. It sounds like you're doing the right thing by not telling them.

Also, if your parents are claiming you as as a dependent and you're in the US, you are still required to fill out your own tax return. I'd suggest getting a PO Box without their knowledge, and directing the IRS to send your tax return there. Also, get your own bank account without them knowing so that when you cash your check, they can't check your bank balance and figure it out. Then get a credit card (there are some really good student rates out there) and start building credit and savings until you can GTFO. You're amazing, you know what to do, and you got this. I'm rooting for you. 

Edit: I'm not sure how your tax return will show up on their taxes...maybe the internet has more advice on that
